definition: Additional or diverse international links (a second submarine cable, cross-border routes, a second landing station). Choose this for any redundancy of international connectivity.
Physically separate domestic paths, rings or loops so that one cut does not isolate a site or region. Does not include international links or a backup link by another technology.
A secondary link by a different technology (satellite or microwave backing up fibre) that takes over when the main link fails. Does not include a second path of the same technology.
Using more than one provider or operator so that one provider's failure does not cut service. Does not include technical route or link redundancy.

Two or more independent communications links to a critical facility (an emergency centre, a hospital, a data centre) so that its service continues if one fails. Does not include backbone or international routes.
Duplicate critical nodes, network operations centres, exchange points or interconnection points. Does not include links or routes.
Provides alternative connectivity through a different transmission technology
